Change in genetic distance across an MLPE pairwise covariate contrast

Source: R/mlpe_response_change.R
mlpe_response_change.Rd

Computes the expected change in the genetic-distance response associated with changing one or more pairwise covariates in an mlpe_covariates measurement model. This is useful for interpreting IBE coefficients, which are profiled nuisance parameters rather than conductance-surface coefficients.

Usage

mlpe_response_change(
  object,
  covariate = NULL,
  probs = c(0.1, 0.9),
  values = NULL,
  conf.level = 0.95
)

Arguments

object

A fitted terradish model whose measurement model was created with mlpe_covariates.

covariate

Optional character vector naming the pairwise covariates to summarize. Defaults to all pairwise covariates stored in the measurement model.

probs

Numeric vector of length two giving the lower and upper quantiles used to define the contrast when values is NULL. Defaults to the 10th and 90th percentiles.

values

Optional numeric vector of length two giving explicit lower and upper covariate values for a single covariate. Alternatively, provide a named list with one length-two numeric vector per covariate.

conf.level

Confidence level for the Wald confidence interval.

Value

A data frame with one row per covariate and columns describing the low and high covariate values, the contrast, estimated response-scale change, confidence limits, and confidence level.

Details

For a model fitted with mlpe_covariates(), the pairwise mean structure includes terms of the form \(\gamma Z_{ij}\). This function reports \(\gamma (z_{\mathrm{high}} - z_{\mathrm{low}})\), the expected response-scale change in genetic distance across the requested covariate contrast, conditional on the fitted conductance surface.

The interval uses the conditional standard error for the MLPE covariate coefficient from summary(object) and treats the selected covariate contrast as fixed. The reported contrast is a conditional association under the fitted MLPE model. It is not a causal effect or proof that IBE has been separated from IBR or other spatially correlated predictors.

Worked examples

vignette("v08-ibe-ibr-workflow", package = "terradish").

See also

mlpe_covariates, pairwise_endpoint_covariates, terradish

Other inference and model comparison: aic_table(), terradish_cv_folds(), terradish_folds(), terradish_ibe_ratio(), terradish_inference, terradish_rescale_nu()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

# site-level altitude, turned into a pairwise |difference| IBE predictor
site_altitude <- data.frame(
  altitude = terra::extract(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude), coords)[, 2])
g_joint <- mlpe_covariates(site_altitude)

# joint isolation by environment and isolation by resistance
fit_joint <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,
                       conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
                       measurement_model = g_joint)

# Expected change in genetic distance across the covariate's 10th-to-90th
# percentile spread, on the response scale rather than the log scale.
change <- mlpe_response_change(fit_joint)
change
#>          covariate        low      high  contrast   estimate   conf.low
#> 1 absdiff_altitude 0.02037562 0.5275703 0.5071947 0.03288384 0.02661041
#>    conf.high conf.level
#> 1 0.03915727       0.95

# A narrower, interquartile contrast
mlpe_response_change(fit_joint, probs = c(0.25, 0.75))
#>          covariate     low      high  contrast   estimate   conf.low  conf.high
#> 1 absdiff_altitude 0.08377 0.3477135 0.2639435 0.01711271 0.01384802 0.02037739
#>   conf.level
#> 1       0.95
# }
